confidence_story: Textbook folded enzyme; expect uniformly high pLDDT. The control case.
Two EF-hand lobes joined by a flexible linker; expect high pLDDT within lobes but high PAE between them - the domain orientation is genuinely uncertain.
Folded DNA-binding domain flanked by disordered N- and C-termini; expect a sharp confidence cliff at the boundaries. Same protein you scored variants in last lab.
7-transmembrane GPCR; ESMFold handles the bundle well but loops and the C-terminal tail may wobble.
A domain cut out of a larger protein; compare your prediction to the same residues in the full-spike AlphaFold DB model.
Artificial alpha/beta protein with no natural homologs and no AlphaFold DB entry. Watch whether the model trusts a protein evolution never built - and which parts it does not trust.
Intrinsically disordered in solution (Parkinson relevance). Low pLDDT everywhere is the CORRECT answer, not a failure.
Its fold exists only inside the histone octamer (Ch. 4). Predicted alone, the model should show low confidence - a structure that genuinely depends on its binding partners.
